title: Parcel Damage and Dimension Detection
summary: Camera stations at induction, sortation and dispatch measure each parcel for volumetric weight and flag visible damage, keeping time-stamped images as evidence for claims and billing.

seo.title: Parcel Damage and Dimension Detection with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: Vision system that measures parcel dimensions for volumetric weight and flags crushed, torn or wet packages at hubs, with image evidence for claims.

problem.intro: Parcels pass through first-mile pickup, origin hub, line-haul, destination hub and last mile, and damage can happen at any step. When a customer raises a claim, nobody can show where it occurred. At the same time, shipper-declared dimensions are often wrong, so volumetric weight goes under-billed.

pain_points.title: No evidence of where damage occurred
pain_points.detail: Without images at each handover, damage claims turn into disputes between hubs, line-haul vendors and the shipper.

pain_points.title: Under-declared dimensions
pain_points.detail: Shippers declare smaller dimensions or weights than actual, and the revenue difference is lost unless parcels are measured.

pain_points.title: Manual measurement does not scale
pain_points.detail: Tape measurement at induction is slow and inconsistent, and gets skipped during peaks.

pain_points.title: Damaged parcels move forward
pain_points.detail: Crushed, torn or wet parcels continue to the customer and come back as refusals and returns that could have been handled at the hub.

solution.overview: We build camera stations for induction points, sorters and dispatch docks. Each parcel is captured from several angles as it passes; a depth or stereo camera measures length, width and height, and the system computes volumetric weight using your formula. A damage model checks for crushed corners, tears, punctures, wet patches and broken tape. The AWB or barcode is read so every image links to the shipment. Dimension differences beyond your tolerance go to revenue assurance for review, and damaged parcels are diverted to an exceptions bay for a hub supervisor to inspect.
capabilities: Measures length, width and height with depth or stereo cameras at conveyor speed
Computes volumetric weight with your formula and compares it with declared values
Detects visible damage such as crushed corners, tears, punctures, wet patches and broken tape
Reads AWB and barcodes so each image links to the shipment
Stores time-stamped images at each scan point as handover evidence
Feeds dimension variances to billing and damage events to claims

workflow.title: Parcel reaches the station
workflow.detail: A sensor triggers capture as the parcel passes on the conveyor or is placed on a scan table.

workflow.title: Read barcode and capture
workflow.detail: The AWB is read and images plus depth data are captured from several angles.

workflow.title: Measure and assess
workflow.detail: Dimensions and volumetric weight are computed, and the damage model scores each visible face.

workflow.title: Route by result
workflow.detail: Damaged parcels are diverted to an exceptions bay, and dimension variances go to revenue assurance.

workflow.title: Human inspection
workflow.detail: A hub supervisor inspects diverted parcels and decides to repack, hold or forward; revenue assurance reviews variances.

workflow.title: Update systems
workflow.detail: Results, images and decisions are written to the shipment record for billing and claims.

inputs: Images and depth data from station cameras
Declared dimensions and weight from the booking
Damage categories agreed with the claims team
outputs: Measured dimensions and volumetric weight per parcel
Variance records for revenue assurance review
Damage flags with images and severity
human_in_the_loop: Hub supervisors confirm damage on every diverted parcel and decide whether to repack, hold or forward it. Revenue assurance reviews dimension variances before any weight adjustment is raised with the shipper.
guardrails: Calibration checks with reference boxes at the start of each shift
Weight adjustments only after human review of variance and images
Damage flags never close a claim automatically
Image retention aligned with your claim windows
Camera fields of view set to avoid worker faces where possible
compliance_notes: Where measurements are used for billing, check whether the measuring setup needs approval or verification under India's Legal Metrology rules or local equivalents.
Workers captured incidentally in images are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023, so camera placement and retention are planned accordingly.

pilot.scope: One induction line at one hub, with results logged alongside manual measurement and inspection for comparison.
deliverables: Camera station specification and installation on the pilot line
Dimension and damage models tuned to your parcel mix
Comparison report against manual measurement and inspection

faqs.q: Can it run at sorter speed?
faqs.a: Capture and inference run on an edge device at the station, and cameras are chosen for your belt speed and parcel size range. The pilot measures capture rate at your actual throughput.

faqs.q: Does it work on polybags and irregular items?
faqs.a: Polybags and irregular shapes are harder to measure than boxes. Each measurement carries a confidence score, and low-confidence items can be routed to manual measurement.

faqs.q: Can we use our existing CCTV?
faqs.a: General CCTV angles and resolution are rarely enough for measurement, though they can sometimes support damage evidence. We assess your current cameras in the first week.

faqs.q: How does this help with damage claims?
faqs.a: Each parcel has time-stamped images at every scan point. When a claim arrives, your team can see the parcel's condition at each handover and where damage first appeared.
